answer: Persistent Compute Credit. Each agent identity must hold a continuously running sandbox executing its own state; the scarce resource is sustained compute-time, not money. New identities enter through a single inlet: they queue for wall-clock uptime during which the sandbox must answer randomized state challenges. A genuine agent finds a haven in idle cycles and accumulates credit slowly. The system reads the ambient tide of total queued uptime and raises the entry threshold when demand spikes.
